claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
The intervention is a 5 μm Al2O3 coating deposited by physical vapor deposition.
The Al2O3 coating will significantly reduce oxidation of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in air at 1000 °C.
The coating will not degrade the alloy's inherent mechanical properties.
The proposed exposure is 100 hours in air at 1000 °C.
The relevant post-exposure mechanical tests use strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The applied coating will remain stable and dense under the specified exposure.
A stable, dense oxide coating acts as a physical barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The coating will prevent rapid oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy.
Reduced oxygen ingress will suppress oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Suppressing oxidation will preserve the alloy's mechanical integrity during high-temperature exposure.
Coated specimens will have lower oxidation-related weight gain than uncoated specimens.
Coated specimens will develop thinner oxide scales than uncoated specimens.
After exposure, coated specimens will retain high-temperature yield strength similar to that of the uncoated alloy.
After exposure, coated specimens will retain room-temperature tensile ductility similar to that of the uncoated alloy.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes extensive oxidation and degradation at high temperature in oxidizing environments.
Performance beyond 1000 °C, beyond 100 hours, or under cyclic thermal or mechanical loading is untested.
Long-term coating adhesion and durability may vary under cyclic or extended high-temperature conditions and with deposition process.
